results.content: *LinkDaddy LLC has launched certificatesofconformity.co.za, the first independent vault for South Africa's mandatory pre-export verification programme that begins enforcement on 20 September 2026 for Mainland China imports across solar PV, furniture, cosmetics, toys, and electrical appliances.*. Clearwater, United States, May 2, 2026 -- CLEARWATER, Florida — LinkDaddy LLC has launched certificatesofconformity.co.za, the first independent vault for South Africa's mandatory pre-export verification programme that begins enforcement on 20 September 2026 for Mainland China imports across solar PV, furniture, cosmetics, toys, and electrical appliances. The company operates a regulatory infrastructure network spanning South African import compliance, EU export compliance through digitalproductpassports.co.za, and identity-anchoring infrastructure through kycregistry.co.za. LinkDaddy LLC is a Florida-registered company headquartered in Clearwater, founded by Anthony James Peacock to build documentation infrastructure for mandatory regulatory regimes that governments mandate but do not themselves host. The company operates a network of regulatory compliance vaults serving South African importers, EU exporters, and African trade participants.

results.title: Multi-millionaire Arthur Eze’s Oranto faces fresh setback as South Sudan cancels oil licence over stalled exploration - Business Insider Africa
results.content: South Sudan has declined to renew the Block B3 exploration licence held by Oranto Petroleum, citing years of inactivity, including the failure to conduct seismic surveys, drill any wells, or meet key financial obligations since 2017, according to the Ministry of Petroleum. * Oranto has faced a series of licence cancellations and disputes in other African markets, including Senegal and Equatorial Guinea. South Sudan has declined to renew the Block B3 exploration licence held by Oranto Petroleum, citing years of inactivity, including the failure to conduct seismic surveys, drill any wells, or meet key financial obligations since 2017, according to the Ministry of Petroleum. In recent years, the company has also faced licence cancellations and disputes across several African markets, raising concerns over its execution record in upstream oil and gas projects. Industry analysts note that Oranto has historically pursued a pan-African exploration strategy, acquiring early-stage licences and partnering with larger international oil companies to develop them.
